narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate how central banks have significantly lowered interest rates to stimulate the economy, particularly highlighting the sharp decline following the 2008 financial crisis and subsequent further reductions.

units.meaning: The Bank of England base rate is dramatically lower than its 1991 peak: it starts at 13.87% in 1991 and later reaches 0.25%.

basis.note: highest value in the table; start of the Bank Rate series
final low in the Bank Rate series

accepted_routes: fell from an early 13.87% peak to a 0.25% low
the Bank Rate ends far below its 1991 high
units.visual_evidence_rule: The Bank Rate line must show an early high at 13.87% and a final low at 0.25%.
units.temporal_anchor: the opening clause about lowering interest rates
units.reviewer_question: Must the clip show both the 1991 13.87% high and the final 0.25% low, or is the overall decline enough without both endpoints?

units.meaning: During the financial-crisis period, the Bank of England base rate dropped sharply from 5.00% to 0.50%, a 4.50 percentage-point cut.

basis.note: value immediately before the sharp drop

units.visual_evidence_rule: A steep downward segment from 5.00% to 0.50% must be visible on the Bank Rate line.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 5.00% starting point of the sharp decline required, or can the clip just show the fall to 0.50%?

weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
